newsitem.title: CHILE: Massad becomes Chilean Central Bank president.
newsitem.headline: Massad becomes Chilean Central Bank president.

text.p: The Chilean government published the resolution naming economist Carlos Massad as the new president of the Central Bank.
The resolution, published in the official daily gazette, confirms Massad's appointment by President Eduardo Frei as a member of the bank's five-member board and its president.

The Senate approved Massad's appointment last week over the objections of some rightist legislators, who charged that he was too close to Frei's Christian Democratic Party to guarantee the bank's independence.

Massad replaced Roberto Zahler, who quit in June after accusing the board of granting too many concessions to private banks in their negotiations to reschedule payments on their debts with the Central Bank.
Massad, a former health minister under Frei and a Central Bank president in the late 1960s, said last week he would complete Zahler's term to late 1997 and possibly stay in the post beyond then.
